slides.title: Operating System Introduction
content: An Operating System (OS) is system software that manages hardware and software resources and acts as an interface between the user and the computer
It enables applications to run, manages files, and controls devices like CPU, memory, and input/output systems
It simplifies user interaction by providing graphical or command-line interfaces
Without an OS, users would have to directly control hardware, making computing complex and inefficient

slides.title: Core Functions of OS
content: Process management creates, schedules, and terminates processes while allocating CPU time efficiently
Memory management allocates and deallocates memory to ensure programs run without interference
File system management organizes data into files and directories for easy access and storage
Device management controls hardware devices like printers, disks, and input/output systems
Security and access control protect data and ensure only authorized users can access resources

slides.title: Program vs Process vs Thread
content: A program is a static set of instructions stored on disk that becomes active only when executed
A process is a program in execution that includes code, memory, CPU state, and allocated resources
A thread is the smallest unit of execution within a process that shares memory but runs independently
Threads improve performance, responsiveness, and parallel execution within applications

slides.title: Types of Operating Systems
content: Operating systems are categorized based on their functionality, hardware usage, and application requirements
Batch OS processes jobs in groups without user interaction, suitable for large-scale computations
Multiprogramming and multitasking OS allow multiple programs to run efficiently by sharing CPU time
Multiprocessing OS uses multiple CPUs to execute tasks simultaneously for high performance
Distributed OS manages multiple computers as a single system for scalability and resource sharing

slides.title: Batch & Multiprogramming OS
content: Batch operating systems group similar jobs into batches and execute them sequentially without user interaction
They improve throughput but have long execution time and lack flexibility
Multiprogramming OS keeps multiple programs in memory and switches CPU when one waits for I/O
This improves CPU utilization and system efficiency by reducing idle time

slides.title: Multiprocessing & Distributed OS
content: Multiprocessing OS uses multiple processors to execute tasks in parallel, improving speed and reliability
It includes symmetric multiprocessing (equal processors) and asymmetric multiprocessing (master-slave model)
Distributed OS connects multiple independent systems and manages them as a single system
It provides scalability, fault tolerance, and resource sharing across multiple machines
